I'm a 50-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with middle school education, and I've been working my family's land for over three decades. We have about 8 mu of good flat land here on the North China Plain, and like most folks in my village, I stick to the wheat-maize double cropping system. It's tight — harvest wheat in early June and plant maize almost the same week — but two crops a year is how we survive. I don't have money to gamble on new crops, and I don't need to.

This October I'm putting winter wheat on all 8 mu. I'll buy improved seed — probably *luyuan502* or *jimai22* from the dealer. I tried saving my own seed a few years back and the yield dropped, so now I pay for fresh seed every couple of years. I'll rotary till first to break up the maize stubble left in the field, then sow in early October while the soil still has some moisture from the autumn rains.

For fertilizer, the extension agent told me 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is the recommendation, but last year I applied around that and the wheat looked a bit pale at jointing. This year I'm putting down about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu — I spread compound fertilizer before sowing and then topdress with urea at jointing. I figure it's better to waste a few yuan on extra fertilizer than to lose half a harvest. The compound bag gives me some phosphorus and potassium too, maybe 8 kg and 4 kg per mu. I don't calculate it precisely; I go by bags per mu, same as my neighbors.

I'll irrigate three times: a winter irrigation before the hard freeze to protect the seedlings, one at jointing in March, and one during grain filling in May if the rains don't come. Pumping water costs electricity, but three times is what everyone around here does. For chemicals, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring and insecticide twice — once for aphids and again later if something else shows up. Three pesticide rounds total.

Come June, the wheat comes off and there's no time to plough. I'll plant summer maize no-tillage directly into the stubble, using a hybrid like *denghai605*. The seed dealer says these hybrids give 500 kg per mu or more if the weather holds, and I've seen it happen. For the maize, I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting — about 16 kg nitrogen per mu — and irrigate twice over the summer, usually at silking and grain filling. Herbicide once at the start, insecticide twice for corn borer. I expect about 450 kg per mu from the wheat and 500 kg per mu from the maize. That's my plan. It's not fancy, but it feeds my family.
